papers.title: A data-driven approach for learning traffic assignment using an artificial neural network
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Civil Engineers - Transport
papers.abstract: Solving transportation network design problems using traffic assignment models becomes increasingly impractical as the size of the considered network grows, due to the need to evaluate numerous candidate solutions. This study aims to model the traffic assignment process through a data-driven approach, and introduces a model based on an artificial neural network (ANN) to predict the total travel time in a network under various link capacity modifications for a specified set of links. ANN-based prediction models are trained and validated on a synthetic data set generated from a medium-sized network to evaluate the feasibility of the proposed approach. Models developed using different ANN architectures highlight the importance of selecting the most suitable architecture specific to the problem. The practical value of the ANN-based prediction model becomes apparent when used in optimising a transportation network design problem instead of the traditional traffic-assignment model: the ANN-based model reduced by up to 60 000 times the computation time required for the optimisation.

papers.title: Toward Lifecycle-Ready Digital Twins For Facility Technical Management
papers.abstract: Digital twins are increasingly promoted as a means to address persistent challenges in the built environment, yet their role in maintenance-focused facility management (FM) remains underexplored. This article explores the practical integration of digital twins into facility technical management through a real-life case environment involving three operational buildings and a two-year deployment period. Using a mixed-method approach combining surveys, interviews, operational observations, and industry feedback, the study investigates the organizational, technical, and information-management-related factors affecting the implementation and usability of BIM-based digital twins in maintenance operations.The findings identify key requirements related to BIM data structures, information management practices, naming conventions, and the involvement of maintenance stakeholders during the design and handover phases. Based on the case findings, the article outlines a four-step BIM process development framework and a four-step BIM enablement framework for facility technical management.The study further highlights the importance of user-friendly graphical user interfaces (GUIs) in bridging the gap between design-oriented BIM environments and the practical needs of maintenance personnel. The findings suggest that digital twins should be approached as continuously managed lifecycle information assets rather than static handover deliverables. The article contributes practice-oriented insights into how BIM-based digital twins can support information continuity and operational usability in facility technical management contexts.

papers.title: Vehicle dynamics simulation considering multipoint contact between wheel and rail during earthquakes
papers.journal: Proceedings of the Institution of Mechanical Engineers Part F Journal of Rail and Rapid Transit
papers.abstract: Large earthquakes occurred repeatedly in Japan, and, in some cases, railway vehicles derailed and overturned during earthquakes. Safety measures are being implemented in various railway sectors, and it is important to continue investigating ways to improve safety. The vehicle dynamics simulator (VDS) developed by Railway Technical Research Institute (RTRI) has been used to analyze the behavior of railway vehicles in the event of earthquakes; however, this simulation program has some limitations in terms of the wheel-rail contact problem, which is essential for the vehicle dynamics of rolling stocks due to the performance limitations of the computers at that time. This study developed a new simulation program, i.e., the VDS-X, which includes a multipoint-contact-capable online contact calculation algorithm, thereby enabling analyses that consider the changes in contact conditions that were not fully considered by conventional methods. Using the VDS-X, the results of safety limits for sinusoidal excitations are compared with those obtained by the conventional VDS, and the differences in wheelset behavior between stopped and running conditions are investigated. The results confirm that the trends in safety limits were reproduced in a manner consistent with the conventional method. Furthermore, a detailed analysis of the contact state revealed fundamental differences in the wheel-rail contact behavior during the stopped and running conditions. The behavior under the stopped condition involves repeated two-point contact. In contrast, under the running condition, the influence of the wheel flange attempting to climb onto the rail becomes more pronounced. This indicates a correlation with a reduction in the safety limit. These results provide a new interpretation of reduced safety margins under running conditions, which has previously been observed at a macroscopic level through simulations, from the perspective of wheel-rail contact issues. The findings of this study demonstrate the importance of wheel-rail contact models of rolling stock during earthquakes.

papers.title: Comprehensive energy efficiency assessment and validation of ship shaft generator and hydrodynamic energy-saving systems under actual operating conditions
papers.abstract: Widely used energy efficiency indicators, including the Energy Efficiency Design Index (EEDI), Energy Efficiency Existing Ship Index (EEXI), and Carbon Intensity Indicator (CII), have limitations in assessing the comprehensive energy efficiency of ocean-going ships under actual operating conditions at the design stage. To address this issue, this study proposes an engineering assessment framework for shaft generator and hydrodynamic energy-saving systems and introduces the Energy Efficiency Comprehensive Index (EECI), which incorporates typical shipping routes and actual marine environments. An extendable mathematical model of the ship power system and energy-saving devices is developed and validated against actual operational data. Navigational scenarios are then reduced based on correlations among environmental variables to improve computational efficiency. For a 230,000 DWT bulk carrier, factorial analysis shows that the combined application of the shaft generator, PRH retrofit, and propeller tip trimming reduces EECI by 8.23%. Taking the actual operational CII change as the benchmark, EECI reduces the discrepancy in the estimated retrofit benefit by 63.31% compared with EEXI. These results indicate that EECI provides a more representative design-stage assessment of expected operational energy-efficiency benefits, particularly for ships that do not normally operate at the prescribed design point.

papers.title: A Comparative Analysis of the Seismic Performance of Four Buildings Representative of Bagan’s Monumental Heritage
papers.abstract: This paper presents the outcomes of nonlinear static pushover and time history analyses, using both recorded and simulated ground motion signals, on 3D finite element macro-models of four buildings representative of Bagan’s monumental heritage: Myin-pya-gu (1493), Zan-thi (east) (558), Tha-mu-ti-hpaya (844), and Kya-zin-hpaya (1219). The simulations are validated against the observed seismic damage in the 1975 and 2016 earthquakes. The results of the nonlinear finite element method (NLFEM) analyses are complemented by seismic rocking analysis conducted on nonstructural elements, such as spires, through nonlinear kinematic analysis. Analytical estimates of acceleration levels capable of causing shear failure in spires are provided, focusing on elements with a slenderness ratio that makes them vulnerable to shearing rather than rocking (i.e. flexure-controlled) failure modes. A comparative assessment of seismic performance is presented for the four buildings, highlighting the influence of plan symmetry and vertical continuity. These attributes are proposed as key criteria for selecting appropriate retrofit schemes to protect Bagan’s monuments against future seismic events.

papers.title: Beam layout design in shear wall structures using a diffusion model guided by rule-based masks
papers.abstract: Serving as critical load supports and transfer components in shear wall structures, beams require layout designs that balance mechanical rationality with architectural functionality constraints. Conventional design methods, which rely on engineers' expertise, are challenging to systematize and are inherently inefficient. Moreover, existing intelligent design algorithms have attempted to integrate constraints related to architectural space and mechanical topology while delivering sufficiently detailed outputs, ultimately resulting in suboptimal outcomes. To address these challenges, this study synthesizes engineering experience rules pertaining to spatial functionality and load-bearing constraints and encodes them into a mask that delineates potential beam placement locations on a building plan. Subsequently, a diffusion model, well-known for its ability to generate intricate design details, is employed to produce the corresponding beam layout from the image mask. This approach, designated as the mask-constrained diffusion model for beam layout design in shear wall structures, introduces a key innovation: mitigating the uncontrolled generative range typically associated with diffusion models during beam layout configuration. By embedding engineering knowledge into a mask that constrains the diffusion process, the generation boundaries are effectively regulated, ensuring controllable and effective design outcomes. Analysis indicates that the designs produced by the mask-constrained diffusion model surpass the quality of existing intelligent design methods, achieving a relative 35.0% improvement in consistency with engineer-generated designs while concurrently satisfying critical mechanical performance criteria. This study provides a novel perspective on the intelligent design of beam layouts and serves as a valuable reference for the application of diffusion models in the structural design of buildings.

papers.title: A governance-based framework for Blockchain adoption in construction data management
papers.abstract: Construction projects generate extensive project information; however, construction data management (CDM) remains fragmented, insecure, and weakly governed, particularly in developing economies. Empirical evidence on blockchain (BC) as an integrated governance infrastructure for CDM remains limited in such contexts. This study investigates the perceived potential of BC to address CDM challenges in the Sri Lankan construction industry and develops a Blockchain Adoption Decision Framework for Construction Data Management (BADF-CDM). A sequential mixed-method approach was adopted: questionnaire survey of 35 construction and IT professionals, analysed using the Relative Importance Index, followed by 13 semi-structured expert interviews analysed through manual content analysis. Mappings between CDM challenges and BC capabilities, and between adoption barriers and implementation strategies, were reviewed through a focus group discussion and integrated into the BADF-CDM. Limited real-time data access, weak data security, weak version control, and system interoperability emerged as critical CDM challenges. BC capabilities, particularly security, transparency, auditability, immutability, and decentralisation, were perceived as relevant to addressing them. However, adoption depends on organisational readiness, including leadership commitment, technical capability, workforce skills, and regulatory support. BADF-CDM provides an evidence-informed framework for identifying CDM challenges, selecting BC capabilities, assessing adoption barriers, and planning phased adoption.

papers.title: Delay-Compensated MPC for Path Tracking of Articulated Steering Vehicles
papers.journal: Journal of Transportation Engineering Part A Systems
papers.abstract: Abstract Articulated steering vehicles are key equipment for mining transportation, underground roadways, and heavy-duty material handling infrastructure, where insufficient path-tracking accuracy may reduce roadway safety margins and increase the risk of lane encroachment, collision, and traffic interruption in confined haulage corridors. Hydraulic actuator delay is a practical source of steering lag in such vehicles, but it is often simplified or neglected in existing path-tracking control studies. To address this gap, this study develops a delay-compensated model predictive control (MPC) framework by incorporating experimentally identified hydraulic actuator delay into the pre‍dictive control model. Simulation results showed that MPC provided better stability performance than linear quadratic regulator (LQR), reducing sideslip angle, yaw rate, and lateral acceleration by 21%–48% under representative lane-change maneuvers. With actuator-delay compensation, the proposed MPC further reduced the tractor lateral deviation by 53.12% under single lane change (SLC) and 83.63% under double lane change (DLC) conditions. These results indicate that the proposed method can improve the operational safety, tracking reliability, and automation readiness of articulated vehicles used in mining and infrastructure transportation scenarios.

papers.title: In Situ Instrumentation and Calibration of Flexible Pavement Under Real Traffic: Experimental Comparison with the AEMC/MeDiNa Model in Brazil
papers.journal: International Journal of Pavement Research and Technology
papers.abstract: Abstract This article presents the design, calibration and field evaluation of an instrumented flexible pavement section aimed at quantifying mechanical responses and comparing them with the predictions of multilayer elastic analysis (AEMC), the mechanistic component of the Brazilian mechanistic-empirical method MeDiNa. Total earth pressure cells and strain gauges were installed in the asphalt layer, base, sub-base and subgrade to monitor stresses and strains under a controlled loading protocol ranging from 0 to 100% of the 8.2-ton standard axle load, to evaluate conversion factors and verify the metrological stability of the measurements. The results showed physically consistent time histories, with progressive response reduction as the load decreased, spatial sensitivity to wheel path position and stress attenuation with depth. In the model-to-field comparison, the assumptions of full and partial interlayer bonding generally provided better agreement with the measured data than the unbonded scenario, although magnitude discrepancies persisted for some stresses and strains. From an operational standpoint, the study highlighted the critical influence of sensor integrity and redundancy, cable and connection protection and vehicle trajectory control on data quality. As a contribution, the work provides experimental evidence for the evaluation of AEMC/MeDiNa in the Brazilian context and organizes practical recommendations for future instrumentation campaigns and for strengthening the regional calibration of the method.

papers.title: A kinematically-constrained Hankel dynamic mode decomposition for short-term prediction of ship manoeuvring in ambient currents
papers.abstract: The accurate prediction of vessel manoeuvring dynamics is essential for ensuring navigational safety in the transition toward maritime autonomy. In this study, a kinematically-constrained Hankel dynamic mode decomposition (Hankel-DMD) approach is developed to model and predict vessel manoeuvring dynamics. The vessel motion is represented using a state formulation consisting of position and resultant speed, and the Hankel-DMD method, together with a component-wise normalisation of the position states, is used to extract the modes governing the system dynamics. To improve the physical consistency of the prediction, a kinematic constraint linking vessel position and speed is incorporated as a post-processing reconstruction step. The developed approach is examined using the data generated from a physics-based Maneuvering Modelling Group (MMG) manoeuvring model for an azimuth thruster-equipped tug. Three cases are considered, including manoeuvring in calm water, in the presence of ambient current along the X -direction (following), and current along the Y -direction (cross). Quantitative error metrics show that the kinematically-constrained reconstruction reduces the trajectory RMSE by 71% in calm water (from 1.09 m to 0.31 m) and by 60% for the following current (from 7.31 m to 2.90 m). For the cross current, however, the XY-normalised pure Hankel-DMD prediction achieves the slightly lower RMSE (1.34 m versus 2.80 m for the constrained reconstruction), indicating that the benefit of the kinematic constraint is scenario-dependent. These findings demonstrate that incorporating a kinematic constraint can improve the robustness of data-driven vessel trajectory prediction, although its benefit is case-dependent under environmental disturbances.

papers.title: Applicability assessment of an improved identification method for asphalt mixture meso-structure based on digital image processing technology
papers.abstract: Digital image processing (DIP) technology provides an effective approach for characterising the mesostructure of asphalt mixtures. However, existing DIP-based methods still face challenges in effectively removing interference information and accurately segmenting adherent regions in asphalt mixture images. In this study, an improved mesostructure identification method, consisting of a low-frequency component averaging mapping-based preprocessing method and a shape feature parameter-assisted adherent region segmentation method, was proposed and its applicability was systematically evaluated. The results demonstrate that, compared with conventional preprocessing methods, the proposed preprocessing method can effectively correct uneven illumination, improve grayscale consistency, enhance image details and suppress interference information while preserving mesostructural features. Furthermore, compared with the conventional watershed method, the proposed adherent region segmentation method effectively reduces under-segmentation errors and accurately identifies aggregates containing internal bright or dark regions. The proposed method exhibits comparable performance to the watershed method for asphalt mixtures with smaller nominal maximum aggregate sizes (NMAS), while achieving higher aggregate recognition accuracy for mixtures with larger NMAS. These findings demonstrate that the proposed method provides a reliable and robust approach for asphalt mixture mesostructure identification, although its applicability to specimens with relatively small NMAS requires further investigation.
